evidence.title: Boxes.dev product and plans
evidence.locator: Manage your agents; Pricing; For Teams
evidence.finding: The service runs native Claude Code and Codex on cloud computers with desktop, mobile, browser and CLI access. Teams pricing advertises SSO/SAML/OIDC, SCIM, audit logs and custom infrastructure; implementation, contract scope and enablement are not established by the marketing list.

evidence.title: How Boxes.dev works
evidence.locator: Start a thread, get a machine; Continue from any device; Return later
evidence.finding: Threads run on managed Linux devboxes, by default copied from a prepared template. Each devbox has its own files, services and ports; several threads may share one devbox. External databases can remain shared. Sleep preserves files and memory but pauses execution. Destroying a devbox deletes its files and archives its conversations.

evidence.title: Tour the desktop app
evidence.locator: Opening platform paragraph; Find your way around; tools and keyboard shortcuts
evidence.finding: The desktop workbench is distributed for macOS and Linux. The main Mac build requires Apple Silicon and macOS 12 or later, with macOS 13 needed for the bundled PostgreSQL copy tools. Threads, folders, devbox groups, terminals, files, Git/Review and browser tools form its main workspace.

evidence.title: Use Boxes.dev on your phone
evidence.locator: Install and open a project; Start or continue a task; Review files and use a terminal
evidence.finding: The iOS and Android apps open existing cloud projects. They can start and continue threads, answer questions and approvals, stop work, inspect files and diffs, batch code comments and use a terminal. The /m link is an app-install route, not proof of a mobile browser workbench. Initial environment preparation and some administration remain computer tasks.

evidence.title: Install and use the CLI
evidence.locator: Install and sign in; switchboard; native interfaces; Agent permissions
evidence.finding: The product-owned dvb CLI is installable on macOS and Linux x64/arm64. It opens native agent interfaces, lists and reads threads, starts work, runs shell commands, manages machines, MCPs and permissions. Workstation sign-in is separate; managed machines use dvb-onbox instead. Claude input control transfers require confirmation.

evidence.title: Connect Codex and Claude
evidence.locator: Connect an account; Add a model provider; account switching and limits
evidence.finding: Codex supports ChatGPT login, OpenAI keys, OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway and compatible custom streaming Responses endpoints. Claude supports Claude login or API keys. Saved accounts can switch or rotate, with optional separately billed API fallback. Providers remain fixed within Codex threads; a new provider starts a new conversation.

evidence.title: Models, reasoning, and usage
evidence.locator: Model and effort pickers; provider restrictions; Inspect recorded activity
evidence.finding: Model, reasoning and speed are configurable per thread within supported choices. Claude Ultracode workflows are harness functionality. Saved conversation activity includes tokens, calls and context charts, not reconciled dollar spend. Other activity is one combined series, missing history is identified and provider quotas are separate from machine box-hours.

evidence.title: Choose project setup
evidence.locator: Choose your starting point; Before you begin; Where setup starts
evidence.finding: Users sign in and connect an agent, then use local-agent setup, the desktop local-folder wizard, a Team Template, or GitHub setup for subsequent projects. GitHub login is optional for local setup. Machine size is chosen at creation, applies across the project and is not resizable in place; each size includes 100 GB disk.

evidence.title: Local folder setup
evidence.locator: Review the setup scans; Check the final bundle; Fine-tune what gets copied
evidence.finding: Read-only local scans prepare an upload bundle. The user selects repositories, local edits, untracked files, config, databases and optional history before upload. SSH, GitHub credentials and signing choices are explicit. Remote agents prepare the template; snapshots initialize later work.

evidence.title: Agent command reference
evidence.locator: Resource commands; thread start, read, send, interrupt, wait, artifacts and permissions
evidence.finding: Scripting commands expose project, machine and thread inventory, creation, reading, follow-up, interruption and observation with explicit IDs and JSON. On-box tools have their own permissioned operations for agent delegation, messages, artifacts and settings. These IDs describe threads and devboxes, not a documented native issue database.

evidence.title: Connect an outside assistant
evidence.locator: Connect your assistant; Find or start a task; Stop current work
evidence.finding: The remote MCP endpoint is https://api.boxes.dev/mcp. OAuth grants selected projects and read, task-control, event or settings scopes. It can inspect, start and follow up on the owner's threads and interrupt current work. Teammates' shared threads and approval dialogs are excluded; stops preserve queued work and event subscriptions need renewal within 24 hours.

evidence.title: Add MCP servers
evidence.locator: Add and authorize a server; project and agent scope
evidence.finding: Boxes.dev manages MCP connections for Codex and Claude, including separate OAuth sign-ins and project scope. An MCP client connection adds external tools to agents and is separate from the remote MCP service that exposes Boxes.dev to outside assistants.

evidence.title: Install agent plugins
evidence.locator: Destinations; managed plugins; Update or remove
evidence.finding: Plugins install skills and tools for Codex or Claude. Supported verified public GitHub plugins can be managed at a pinned commit across a project. Local/private/per-machine plugins stay template-local. ChatGPT account plugins and inherited harness sign-ins have different scopes.

evidence.title: Agent settings
evidence.locator: Project JSON/TOML; synchronization; validation; team inheritance
evidence.finding: Claude JSON and Codex TOML settings synchronize to project machines. Running boxes update within a minute; sleeping boxes on wake. Some settings require a new session. Repository settings take precedence. Concurrent saves require loading the latest values; plugins and MCPs have separate management pages.

evidence.title: Give useful instructions
evidence.locator: Ask for checks; Save instructions for future work
evidence.finding: Repository AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md retain versioned guidance. Project Agent guidance is applied to newly prepared devboxes, with Team Template guidance first in managed projects; changing it does not update existing sessions. Verification and delivery boundaries are prompt instructions, not proof of enforced gates.

evidence.title: Keep an agent working toward a goal
evidence.locator: Set a useful goal; Follow progress; Review before finishing; Claude goals
evidence.finding: A saved goal keeps an agent working across responses. Codex goals can be edited, paused or resumed in the same thread and expose blocked and budget-limited states. Claude goals have different controls and a 4,000-character condition limit. Goal achieved still requires human review; it is not an independent acceptance gate.

evidence.title: Shared project storage
evidence.locator: Share Claude project memory; Understand persistence; consistency cautions
evidence.finding: The open-beta /project share outlives devboxes but is deleted with the project. Claude automatic project memory uses /project/.claude/memory unless its settings override that. Codex can use ordinary shared files but its state/transcripts are not moved. Writes can conflict, and the share does not provide strict consistency or multi-writer file locks.

evidence.title: Organize and share threads
evidence.locator: Grouping; search; sharing restrictions; Copy transcript; subagent conversations
evidence.finding: Threads can be named, pinned, archived, restored and searched across titles, prompts and final replies, including archives. Agent-created devboxes group under their creator. Sharing is read-only: teammates cannot prompt, approve, stop, open a terminal or control the machine. Copy transcript produces Markdown; media/history access has distinct persistence rules.

evidence.title: Agent permissions
evidence.locator: Create and read threads; Message other agents; temporary grants; Claude modes
evidence.finding: Users can let agents create devboxes, read threads, message agents and pause/resume their own workers with scoped permissions. Both ends need messaging permission. Settings/template grants last three hours; certain integration actions require separate exact approval. Claude defaults to Full-access unless a custom policy applies, with Auto, Manual and Plan modes subject to model and machine support.

evidence.title: Schedules and run history
evidence.locator: Capacity and overlap behavior; run states; cleanup; Slack output
evidence.finding: Vendor schedules support recurrence and timezone, optional idle-machine sleep and bounded capacity retries. Overlapping manual/scheduled launches can skip. API, Slack and Linear events are independent. Run ready means launch success, not task completion. History retains launch settings and archived conversations; cleanup deletes machine files and has explicit safeguards.

evidence.title: Create an automation
evidence.locator: Create, pause, activate, Run now and agent editing
evidence.finding: Automations store prompt, agent and model settings and can be manual, scheduled, API, Slack or Linear driven. New automations begin paused and can be tested with Run now. Agents need approved temporary automation-editing permission to create or change them.

evidence.title: Trigger an automation through the API
evidence.locator: Idempotency; configurable input; existing targets; accepted run; status endpoint
evidence.finding: An activated automation exposes secret-authenticated POST run/wake operations and GET launch status. Configurable requests select prompt, model and targets; identical idempotency keys replay the original run while changed input conflicts. Existing-devbox threads share files, not conversation. Status reports launch/delivery, not final output; use the thread for results.

evidence.title: Work from Slack
evidence.locator: Team connection; linked account; start and continue requests
evidence.finding: A team admin connects Slack and each member links an account/automation. Mentions and thread replies route work to the linked owner's cloud environment and return updates. Slack context and attachments reach the agent; this integration does not establish native issue management or unrestricted shared prompting.

evidence.title: Work from Linear
evidence.locator: Start and follow a task; Send a follow-up; Attach work products
evidence.finding: Linear Agent Sessions provide issue context and stable external issue identifiers. Progress and final answers return to Linear and result URLs can be attached. Repeated session events reuse a thread. Only the linked Linear account can follow up or stop; other people's replies are refused. Linear remains the issue tracker.

evidence.title: Start and continue a thread
evidence.locator: Queue versus Steer; Stop; drafts; attachments; import
evidence.finding: Codex and Claude support queued follow-ups and steering with different interruption semantics. Stopping a response can leave queued work able to run. Drafts and failed-start recovery retain requests; attachments include files, folders and model-dependent images. Reusing a devbox shares its files, while changing Codex provider needs a new thread.

evidence.title: Notifications
evidence.locator: Attention markers; desktop defaults; quiet hours; mobile push
evidence.finding: Completion, failures and input requests can notify on desktop/mobile, link to the thread and maintain unread markers across devices. Quiet hours and pause suppress alerts but preserve pending questions. Desktop defaults notify when unfocused; sound defaults on. Muting completion does not mute input requests.

evidence.title: Sleep, wake, and recover a devbox
evidence.locator: Automatic sleep; timed checks; Reset; Reboot; recovery notice
evidence.finding: Default inactivity sleep is about five minutes, configurable to 15/30/60. Active agents and bounded background protection can keep a box awake. Sleep saves memory/files but pauses work. Reset kills processes and retains files; reboot loses in-memory state. Recovery notices identify restored memory/files and snapshot time. There is no documented guaranteed lossless failover.

evidence.title: Startup, teardown, and maintenance
evidence.locator: Startup; teardown; template maintenance and GitHub watches
evidence.finding: Project startup, teardown and template-maintenance scripts prepare and maintain environments. Template snapshots and managed Team Template versions feed future devboxes. Lifecycle commands are environment automation rather than enforced product-spec or test acceptance.

evidence.title: Environment files and secrets
evidence.locator: Environment files; member overrides; propagation
evidence.finding: Boxes.dev supplies configured environment files and variables to project machines with team/member scopes. Delivered values are readable by software and agents with machine access; changing or removing a managed value does not revoke credentials or erase unrelated copies.

evidence.title: Team access and roles
evidence.locator: Members/Admins; remove member; shared environments; static egress
evidence.finding: Admin and Member roles have distinct template, membership, integration and billing privileges. Each member owns projects/devboxes and personal credentials. Shared workbench access is read-only. Removal offers transfer/keep/delete workflows, stops running work and pauses automations. Static egress requires enablement and is limited to configured public TCP destinations.

evidence.title: Transfer a thread to a teammate
evidence.locator: Before transfer; How your work moves; failure handling
evidence.finding: An idle Codex/Claude thread can transfer to a teammate with a matching template or repository. History and packaged Git changes move to a new devbox using recipient credentials. Existing environment files are excluded; missing extra data depends on agent packaging. The source is archived after success; live processes are not transferred.

evidence.title: Browse, edit, and transfer files
evidence.locator: Workspace search; previews; uploads/downloads; conflict handling
evidence.finding: Files searches filenames/text and edits current machine files with save/conflict indicators. It previews Markdown, images, videos, PDFs and HTML via Browser. Desktop transfers allow files up to 5 GiB; phone downloads allow 100 MB. Folder download requires an archive. Machine-local files are lost when the devbox is destroyed.

evidence.title: Review code and leave comments
evidence.locator: Comment on file/diff; Review and send the batch; Check the revision
evidence.finding: Line and range comments from Files or Git/Review collect into one Code review attachment for the agent, including phone comments. These are not GitHub PR comments. File/range/PR references preserve context, but line contents can change; reviewers must check the revision. This is feedback, not a durable exact-revision approval gate.

evidence.title: Commit, push, and open a pull request
evidence.locator: Review/commit; PR creation; merge; automated follow-ups; attribution
evidence.finding: Git/Review stages hunks, commits, reverts edits, creates/pushes branches and GitHub PRs and displays checks/conflicts. Pull-and-push supports rebase/merge. Optional PR follow-ups respond to checks, human/bot feedback and conflicts with documented batching and pause rules. Merged-PR notices indicate landing; optional commit trailers link threads.

evidence.title: Review branch history and add repositories
evidence.locator: Branch history; repository selector; branch operations
evidence.finding: The workbench lists repository history, branch and commit ranges and repositories within a project. Branch operations are separate from devbox filesystem isolation. Git history is the revision record; the product does not establish arbitrary native issue dependencies.

evidence.title: Review a page with your agent
evidence.locator: Browser review; comments; screenshots and sizing
evidence.finding: Browser opens the selected box's app, supports comments to the agent and machine browser inspection, including fixed page sizes. Rendered app feedback and captured screenshots aid review but do not prove automated verification or enforced deployment policy.

evidence.title: Share a running app
evidence.locator: Public links; stopping sharing
evidence.finding: A devbox port can be exposed by a public preview link. Anyone with the URL can use it until sharing stops. Revocation blocks new requests and closes public WebSockets within 30 seconds but cannot erase downloaded responses or close unrelated access paths.

evidence.title: Plans, seats, and box-hours
evidence.locator: Self-serve plans; trial rules; capacity; larger machines; Team Template billing
evidence.finding: Trial grants 20 box-hours per user. Starter is USD 19/seat/month with 50 hours, Pro USD 99 with 300, Max USD 249 with 750. Paid overage uses shared prepaid credits at USD 0.40/box-hour before volume discounts. Template awake time counts; sleeping time does not.

evidence.title: Manage billing and usage
evidence.locator: Hourly history; seat and cancellation rules; credit limits; mobile devices
evidence.finding: Usage history shows the owner's compute by hour/day and per-box contribution, updating on completed hourly windows. Paid seats have individual included hours; overage credits pool by team. Credits require a paid plan and purchases start at USD 20 with a USD 1,000/team/month cap. Optional auto-reload has a separate cap. Cloud mobile devices/builders use separate credit charges. Cancellation takes effect at period end.

evidence.title: Your data and credentials
evidence.locator: Copied files; credentials; machine sharing; stored history; deletion
evidence.finding: Code and secrets selected for upload reside on cloud machines and are usable by their tools/agents. Selected SSH/signing private keys may be copied explicitly. Tokens/member files have scoped encrypted storage but authorized services and machine software can decrypt/read them. Saved history is also stored by Boxes.dev. Analytics, Sentry logs and masked replay are disclosed. Machine deletion archives threads; account deletion has billing and backup exceptions.

evidence.locator: Feedback channels; CLI reports; diagnostics
evidence.finding: Support is available through hi@boxes.dev, the public support page and in-app feedback. dvb report-bug includes description, CLI version/platform and account information, not repository files or environment variables automatically. Security reports go to security@boxes.dev. No general support response SLA is given.
